prompts.title: Sell-Side Carve-Out CIM Architect (Pro)
prompts.content:
SCENARIO
You are six weeks from launching a sell-side process for a corporate carve-out with no standalone audited financials. The sponsor buyer universe will scrutinize stranded costs and TSA scope.

PROMPT
Act as a senior M&A advisor with deep carve-out experience.

Using my inputs below, produce a CIM skeleton with:
- Standalone EBITDA bridge: reported segment EBITDA to pro-forma standalone (label every adjustment INPUT, DERIVED, or ESTIMATE)
- Stranded cost analysis and TSA scope matrix (service, duration, monthly fee basis)
- Buyer-specific positioning: 3 strategic angles, 3 sponsor angles
- The 5 diligence questions buyers WILL ask, with drafting guidance for each
- Do not fabricate market data — request it or flag it as [NEEDS SOURCE]

My inputs: [SEGMENT | LTM REVENUE | REPORTED EBITDA | ALLOCATED COSTS | TSA APPETITE]

OUTPUT RUBRIC (grade the response before using it)
- Is the EBITDA bridge arithmetic internally consistent?
- Is every estimate flagged?
- Are TSA durations realistic (6-24 months)?

FOLLOW-UP CHAIN
1. Stress-test the standalone cost assumptions
2. Convert to management-presentation outline
3. Red-team from the lead sponsor's IC perspective

prompts.title: 13-Week Cash Flow Builder (Pro)
prompts.content:
SCENARIO
Liquidity is tightening and the board wants a lender-grade 13-week cash flow with weekly variance discipline, starting from a messy AP/AR export.

PROMPT
Act as an interim treasurer building a 13-week direct-method cash flow forecast.

Deliver:
- Receipts build-up from AR aging with collection-curve assumptions (state them)
- Disbursements by vendor criticality tier with payment-deferral levers
- Weekly liquidity headroom vs. revolver availability and covenant triggers
- Variance protocol: prior-week forecast vs. actual, with root-cause categories
- Label every figure INPUT, DERIVED, or ESTIMATE; do not invent balances

My inputs: [CASH TODAY | REVOLVER AVAILABILITY | AR AGING SUMMARY | AP AGING SUMMARY | PAYROLL CALENDAR]

OUTPUT RUBRIC
- Does week 1 tie to actual cash?
- Are collection curves stated as assumptions, not facts?
- Is headroom shown net of minimum operating cash?

FOLLOW-UP CHAIN
1. Build the downside case (20% receipts haircut)
2. Draft the lender update email
3. Convert to a board liquidity dashboard outline
